title: At least one of the odd Riemann zeta values zeta(5), zeta(7), ..., zeta(25) is irrational
author: Wadim Zudilin
work: One of the Odd Zeta Values from zeta(5) to zeta(25) Is Irrational. By Elementary Means
source_version: Official SIGMA 14 (2018) article 028, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2018.028; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
difficulty_reason: The proof builds two coupled hypergeometric linear forms whose half-integer twist cancels the unwanted zeta(3) term. It establishes denominator integrality and synchronized positive-sum asymptotics before obtaining exponential decay faster than the lcm denominator growth. These linked arithmetic and asymptotic constructions are the substantive obligation; the final integer contradiction alone is only their conclusion.

source_check.note: The full original unnumbered main conclusion and complete author proof are retained. All new differentiated partial-fraction denominator bounds, well-poised parity, half-integer twisting and synchronized zeta(3) cancellation are included, together with the positive-summand ratio, unique maximum and paired Stirling asymptotics. The final s=25 integer contradiction uses the explicit decay constant and cited standard prime-number-theorem lcm growth. This is one independent main arithmetic outcome, not four separately counted support lemmas. It identifies no particular irrational value and asserts no independence or strengthened shorter list. Existing approved human statement/proof/context/above-qualification decision copied from the frozen manifest and metadata; no new source or mathematical review.

proof_review.note: The complete eight-page article was read. Lemma1 proves coefficient denominator control by explicit differentiated partial fractions; Lemmas2/3 use well-poised symmetry and integer/half-integer sums to cancel even zeta terms and synchronize the zeta(3) coefficient. Lemma4 supplies the explicit positive-summand ratio, its unique positive maximum equation and Stirling asymptotics for both sums, yielding their ratio limit one. Section4 then uses s=25, the displayed decay constant and prime-number-theorem lcm asymptotics to contradict a positive integer tending to zero. The concentration estimate invokes standard Stirling sum-asymptotic arguments with references and an explicit summand/ratio; this is routine analytic support, not an omitted new arithmetic construction.
